title: The Day the Peepers Started
skyStory: The moon is down to a sixteen percent sliver and still in Pisces, soaking its feet in a tidal pool and refusing to get out. It has decided tonight belongs to the spring peepers, those thumb-sized frogs who shriek like tiny car alarms from every ditch. The moon is their manager. Saturn has asked for a quieter booking. The request has been denied.

reading: Your voice carries further than usual today, Life Path 3. Something you say in passing, half a sentence while pouring coffee, will lodge in somebody's head and stay there until June. Choose the half sentence carefully. Or don't. The universe likes it when you improvise.

The afternoon brings a pileup of small requests, each one polite, each one wanting a piece of you. The [[Six of Pentacles]] reversed is lurking by the photocopier. Give to two of them. Let the third one wait until tomorrow, and notice that the world keeps turning even when you say later.
joel.mission: Tonight, step outside after dark and count the frog voices for one full minute. Report the number to Nancy, rounded wildly up.
joel.omen: A song stuck in your head with the wrong words. Keep the wrong words; they are a message meant for you.

reading: Here is a quiet day with a secret folded into it. The Wood Rat wakes early, notices the light has shifted further north on the kitchen wall, and files that away as evidence. Spring is negotiating in good faith. You are the only one reading the fine print.

Someone will try to rush you before lunch. Smile, keep your pace, finish the sentence you were on. The [[Six of Swords]] wants you rowing at your own tempo, not theirs. By three o'clock the rusher will be asking you what comes next, because you are the one who actually knows.
nancy.mission: Leave one window cracked an inch this evening and listen for the frogs while you do something ordinary.
nancy.omen: A pair of mismatched mittens still hanging on a hook. Winter is saying goodbye; wave back.
nancy.elementWhy: a soft day with soft focus

together.text: Tonight at the same minute, say 9:17, both of you step outside and listen. Frogs, wind, a far-off dog, a car door. Text each other the strangest sound you heard. The peepers will be judging the entries, and they are tough critics.

game.intro: The peepers are back, singing in the ditches like a tiny swamp choir. Saturn wants accompaniment. Count the keys.
game.question: A standard 88-key piano has black keys and white keys. How many of the keys are white?
